questions.stem: An arithmetic series has first term $a$ and common difference $d$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Prove that the sum of the first $n$ terms of the series is
$\frac{1}{2}n[2a+(n-1)d]$.
(4)

$S=\frac{n}{2}[2a+(n-1)d]$ A1 c.s.o
(4)

Must be arithmetic with $a$, $n$ or $d$ or $l$. (+ signs not essential here). 2nd dM1 for adding, must have $2S$ and be a genuine attempt. Either line is sufficient. Dependent on 1st M1. (NB Allow first 3 marks for use of $l$ for last term but as given for final mark.)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
Sean repays a loan over a period of $n$ months. His monthly repayments form an arithmetic sequence.

He repays £149 in the first month, £147 in the second month, £145 in the third month, and so on. He makes his final repayment in the $n$th month, where $n>21$.

(b) Find the amount Sean repays in the 21st month.
(2)

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Over the $n$ months, he repays a total of £5000.
(c) Form an equation in $n$, and show that your equation may be written as
$n^2-150n+5000=0$.
(3)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $S_n=\frac{n}{2}[2\times 149+(n-1)(-2)]$ $(=n(150-n))$ M1 A1
$S_n=5000 \Rightarrow n^2-150n+5000=0$ (*) A1 c.s.o.
(3)
Note (c): M1 for using their $a,d$ in $S_n$. A1 any correct expression. A1cso for putting $S_n=5000$ and simplifying to given expression. No wrong work. NB EPEN has B1M1A1 here but apply marks as M1A1A1 as in scheme.

parts.label: d
parts.text:
(d) Solve the equation in part (c).
(3)

$n=50$ or $100$ A2/1/0
(3)

parts.label: e

questions.stem:
The curve $C$ has equation $y = \frac{1}{3}x^3-4x^2+8x+3$.

The point $P$ has coordinates $(3,0)$.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Show that $P$ lies on $C$.
(1)

parts.label: b
parts.text:
(b) Find the equation of the tangent to $C$ at $P$, giving your answer in the form $y=mx+c$, where $m$ and $c$ are constants.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) $\frac{dy}{dx}=\frac{3}{3}x^2-2\times 4\times x+8$ $(x^2-8x+8)$ M1 A1
When $x=3$, $\frac{dy}{dx}=9-24+8 \Rightarrow m=-7$ M1
Equation of tangent: $y-0=-7(x-3)$ M1
$y=-7x+21$ A1 c.a.o
(5)
Note (b): 1st M1 some correct differentiation ($x^n \to x^{n-1}$ for one term). 1st A1 correct unsimplified (all 3 terms). 2nd M1 substituting $x_P(=3)$ in their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ clear evidence. 3rd M1 using their $m$ to find tangent at $p$. The $m$ must be from their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ at $x_P(=3)$. Use of $\frac{1}{7}$ here scores M0A0 but could get all 3 Ms in Part (c).

parts.label: c
parts.text:
Another point $Q$ also lies on $C$. The tangent to $C$ at $Q$ is parallel to the tangent to $C$ at $P$.
(c) Find the coordinates of $Q$.
(5)
parts.mark_scheme:
(c) $\frac{dy}{dx}=m$ gives $x^2-8x+8=-7$ M1
$(x^2-8x+15=0)$
$(x-5)(x-3)=0$ M1
$x=(3)$ or $5$ A1
$\therefore y=\frac{1}{3}5^3-4\times 5^2+8\times 5+3$ M1
$y=-15\frac{1}{3}$ or $-\frac{46}{3}$ A1
(5)
(11)
Note (c): 1st M1 forming a correct equation "their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ = gradient of their tangent". 2nd M1 for solving a quadratic based on their $\frac{dy}{dx}$ leading to $x=...$. The quadratic could be simply $\frac{dy}{dx}=0$. 3rd M1 for using their $x$ value (obtained from their quadratic) in $y$ to obtain $y$ coordinate. Must have one of the other two M marks to score this.
MR: For misreading $(0,3)$ for $(3,0)$ award B0 and then M1A1 as in scheme. Then allow all M marks but no A ft. (Max 7)
